headline: Approved July 13, 2026 meeting minutes 5-0; public art projects and maintenance were discussed, with no other votes taken.
summary: Members gave updates on funded public art projects, including the Window Wrap, Farmers' Market mural, Zebra Project maintenance, sculpture nameplates, and downtown street art. They discussed removing the Nailed It artwork from 143 Pine Street after the property was sold, and they discussed a maintenance plan and the public art map. The only vote was to approve the prior meeting's minutes.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 13, 2026 meeting by a 5-0 vote.

decision_evidence.quote: Mr. Walsh moved and Ms. Schlachter seconded the motion to approve the committee meeting minutes of July 13, 2026. The vote was (5-0). Motion passed.

plain_text:
1
LEWISTON PUBLIC ART COMMITTEE
Monday, August 10, 2026, at 6:00 pm
Lewiston City Hall, Third Floor Conference Room
Meeting Minutes – FINAL
Committee members in attendance: Darby Ray; James Lysen; Courtney Schlachter; Gerald Walsh; and 
Scott Harriman, Council Liaison.
Committee members absent: Deanna Ehrhardt, Chairperson (excused)
Others present: Kathryn Ruth, Community Development Manager
1) Call Meeting to Order:
In the absence of the Chairperson, Ms. Ray called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm.
2) Approve Meeting Minutes for July 13, 2026
Mr. Walsh moved and Ms. Schlachter seconded the motion to approve the committee meeting 
minutes of July 13, 2026.  The vote was (5-0).  Motion passed.
3) Update on projects funded through the FY26 (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026) Budget
which remain to be finished during the next few months:
a. Window Wrap projects to be designed by local artists $  7,500
b. Lewiston Farmers’ Market Association (LFMA) Mural $12,000
c. Community initiatives $  2,202
Zebra Project Maintenance
       d. Nameplates for 5 sculptures for all costs (design, site visit, $11,697
drawings, materials and installation) plus $200 for drilling
       e.   Street Art and Mitigation of Graffiti in the Downton: $  9,302
1.  Downtown Street Art Project:  $4,302
2.  Marcotte Park – Jude’s Place:  $5,000
Members shared their updates on the projects which were completed or in progress.  These
are very positive and low-cost projects for the community.  All projects had contracts and
payments were processed for the last fiscal year.
Below are brief notes on the projects:
a.  For the Window Wrap projects to be designed by local artists organized and administered by
L/A Arts, also includes the Bus Station and the Hannaford Bus Stop to be addressed.  Mr. Walsh
reported on this project.  While it is behind schedule, it is moving along in a positive fashion.
The final design is available for one location.  The formal review needs to be put together.
There has been back and forth with the parties about details and scheduling.  Some of the
design work has a fun design.  There is a waterfront design that is playful.
b.  The Lewiston Farmers’ Market Mural is moving along well with a lot of comments being
2
expressed.  The artist is working solo on the formal proposal.  There have been a lot of business
comments resulting in design changes.  The Maine Mill is involved.  The Final design will be done
soon and then the colors can be ordered.  The project is not on the calendar yet.  Mr. Walsh is
estimating the project will take place the first week in September, however, it could be a bit
later.  He needs to press on this one.  Colder weather is coming.
c.  The Zebra Project Maintenance requires a lift so originally, it was anticipated that it could be
coordinated with another L/A project, however, this has not come to fruition.  Information will
be going out on social media to alert people to the project.  Everyone at the meeting thought
people would be very interested in this project as it was the beginning of the Public Art
movement in Lewiston.  Serafim Yssolo, the artist who painted the building at Lionel Potvin Park,
will be completing this work later this Summer/Early Fall.  While this maintenance is not
restoration and will not save the art piece indefinitely, it will add some years to its life.  Some
color will be added as needed.
d.  Nameplates for the 5 sculptures project moved forward with the $200 bill for drilling issued.
Both Deputy PW Director Bates and Ms. Ruth continued to work on this project.  Everything had
been installed, however, one of the plaques needed to be moved to the correct location.  This
likely means that there is a plaque in that particular location that also needs to be moved.
This is the culmination of a project that began several years ago.
e.  The Street Art and Mitigation of Graffiti in the Downtown consists of two projects and both 
were awarded to Wicked Illustrations.
1.  Downtown Street Art Project – has been advertised with a request for recommendations for 
locations to mitigate graffiti with butterflies and flowers.  Residents and interested parties were  
invited to Wicked Illustrations to paint the art.  The art will then be installed after the receipt of 
a completed building owner’s permission slip.
2.  Marcotte Park – Jude’s Place – in-studio work started on this project which will take place 
after the downtown art project is underway.  It is likely to be later in August 2026.
       4)   Budget for FY27 (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027)
              For the 4 art projects approved from the Call for Artists, a new agreement needs to be drafted
              as she has been given a Small Project construction type agreement for use.  She will combine
              terms in the PAC regular type of agreement that are needed as it is artwork with the new
              Small Project agreement that the Department will now be using.  Ms. Ruth noted that she is
              handling more work than usual from other positions as there are some vacancies and
              movement in the Department.  She noted that she will get to this as soon as she can.
       5)    Discuss the removal of Public Art – Nailed It – from 143 Pine Street as Public Works has been
               notified that the property has been sold.  While the property has been sold, Public Works is still
mowing it.  The Chairperson followed up on this with the owner to determine details and
if the artwork can stay on site for a while as a new location is needed.  Several locations were
discussed such as Simard Payne Park, Kennedy Park and other areas.  Ms. Ruth brought a list of
city owned vacant lots to the meeting that was passed around for review.  Ms. Ray had
contacted the artist after the last meeting who would like to be involved in the process.  A
              permanent location is needed as well as a plan for funding and/or locating contactor/s who
              would volunteer their services to help out.
3
       6)    Discuss the need for a Maintenance Plan for the City’s Public Art to include when to upkeep and
when to decommission.  Ms. Schlachter reviewed the information she had located due to
her research.  She reviewed a number of websites for best practices and will need to clarify an
approach that would work for Lewiston.  This would include talking to the artists and continuing
to review other cities’ approaches.  She will provide a copy of her research to Ms. Ruth so that
this summary can be included in the meeting minutes.
Projects that have been mentioned that need a maintenance plan and work are the
following:   (a) some of the older sculptures such as Women’s Suffrage which has been
subject to wear; (b) Walking Trees which needs power washing; and (c) the Flags which are
starting to come apart.  There was a discussion about the Walking Tree Structure as it appears
there is spotting and flaking.  It is definitely time to perform maintenance on this piece of art.
       7)    Discussion on the last published list of Public Art financed through the City as well as private
               art.  L/A Arts has this list and had an intern update the electrical boxes with photos from
re-visiting the sites.  While most boxes got a paint update, a few had changes so a new photo 
was needed.  The new Alley murals need to be added.  L/A Arts needs to determine how to label
the art as the map is very crowded in locations.  There was a lengthy discussion about updating 
the map and the plan which can be used to promote Public Art in the City.  This is a work in 
progress and will need some time due to the amount of public art in the city.
8)    Other business, if any, to come before the Committee:
There was no further business.
      9)    Next Meeting:
The next meeting will be held on September 14, 2026 at 6:00 pm at City Hall in the First Floor 
Administrative Conference Room (2nd Monday of the month):
     10)    Motion to adjourn:
Ms. Schlachter moved and Mr. Lysen seconded the motion to adjourn the meeting.  The         
vote was (5-0).  Motion passed.
The Meeting was adjourned at 6:46 pm.
Minutes submitted by:
Kathryn Ruth, Secretary Pro-Tem
